correctness.rationale: For A=0^a1^b and B=1^b0^a with positive a != b, deletion minimality makes each symbol essential to at least one embedding. Both zero and one counts cannot be below 2a and 2b, respectively, because embeddings would then share both symbols in contradictory order; both counts cannot attain the maxima by the essential-position ordering. Thus precisely one type has exactly 2a zeros or 2b ones. The central shared run and forced two boundary letters produce disjoint forms U1^tV and U0^tV, with 1<=t<=b or <=a, respectively. Counting independently constrained U,V gives the two binomial-square terms; unique shortest follows a != b. Independently enumerated deletion-minimal binary words and length histograms for (a,b)=(1,2),(2,1),(2,3),(3,2),(1,4),(2,2); e.g. (2,3) gives 1,5,18 at lengths 7,8,9. The proof handles all positive a,b; finite enumeration alone would not.
